description: At the end of the teaching Arjuna reports: delusion (moha) is destroyed, memory (smṛti) regained through Kṛṣṇa's grace; he stands firm with doubts gone and will do Kṛṣṇa's word (18.73), answering Kṛṣṇa's question whether his confusion born of ignorance is destroyed (18.72).

Sañjaya calls the dialogue wondrous and hair-raising (romaharṣaṇa) (18.74); recalling it again and again he rejoices again and again (18.76); recalling Hari's most wondrous form, great is his amazement (vismaya) and he rejoices again and again (18.77).

Sāttvic happiness, in which one comes to delight through practice and reaches the end of suffering, is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born of the clarity of the self's understanding; rājasic happiness, from the contact of senses and objects, is like nectar at first and poison in the end; tāmasic happiness deludes the self first and last, arising from sleep, sloth and heedlessness (18.36–39).
The one who has become Brahman is serene (prasanna-ātman), neither grieves nor craves, is the same toward all beings, and attains supreme devotion to the Lord (18.54).
The relinquisher (tyāgin), pervaded by sattva, intelligent, with doubts cut away, neither hates disagreeable action nor clings to agreeable action (18.10).
